mainEntity.name: Can I use vinegar to clean my travertine or marble floors?

acceptedAnswer.text: Never — and this is the most common stone cleaning mistake we encounter. Vinegar is acidic and will etch the surface of marble, travertine, and limestone immediately and irreversibly. The dull, hazy spots on stone floors are often acid etch marks from vinegar, citrus cleaners, or toilet bowl cleaner. Only pH-neutral stone-safe cleaners should contact these surfaces.

mainEntity.name: How often should natural stone floors be professionally cleaned in Medford?

acceptedAnswer.text: Once or twice a year for most Medford homes depending on traffic and use. Travertine bathroom floors and entry areas benefit from twice-yearly cleaning due to hard water buildup. Granite countertops may only need annual professional cleaning if maintained well between visits.

mainEntity.name: Do you seal stone after cleaning?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sealing is available as an add-on for porous stones — travertine, limestone, unpolished marble, and slate. It's not required for every stone type; polished granite and honed marble may already have a sealer in good condition. We assess sealer condition during inspection and recommend accordingly.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between stone cleaning and tile and grout cleaning?

acceptedAnswer.text: Stone cleaning focuses on the stone surface using stone-specific pH-neutral chemistry. Tile and grout cleaning addresses the grout lines in tiled surfaces (including stone tile installations). Many stone tile applications benefit from both — we often do them together. See our tile & grout page.

mainEntity.name: Can you clean outdoor stone in the Rogue Valley?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — exterior flagstone, slate steps, and outdoor stone surfaces in Jackson County. Best timing is spring (April–May), after the wet season and before outdoor entertaining begins. Stone with significant organic growth (moss, lichen) is assessed at booking as it may need pre-treatment.

mainEntity.name: Do you clean stone countertops as well as floors?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — kitchen and bathroom countertops, fireplace surrounds, and other stone surfaces, not just floors. Our stone cleaning is a surface service, not limited by location in the home.
